title: Minimum Number of Operations to Make Array Continuous
summary: Given an integer array nums, determine the least number of operations needed to ensure all elements are unique and the difference between the maximum and minimum elements equals the length of the array minus one.
statement: Given an integer array nums, determine the least number of operations needed to ensure all elements are unique and the difference between the maximum and minimum elements equals the length of the array minus one. Each operation allows replacing any element with any integer.
constraints: One operation replaces any element; the final list must contain n distinct consecutive integers.
reference_solution:
def minimum_operations_for_continuous_array(nums):
    n=len(nums);values=sorted(set(nums));left=answer=0
    best=0
    for right,value in enumerate(values):
        while value-values[left]>=n:left+=1
        best=max(best,right-left+1)
    return n-best

hints: Keep the largest set of existing distinct values that fits inside some interval of n consecutive integers.
Sort unique values and use two pointers for windows with max-min<n.
All kept values in such a window can remain while missing positions receive replacements, and no wider-span set can belong to one length-n consecutive target.
